goal: Prove opt-in Rust cuda-oxide ownership of current-C's 128-component eight-warp tensor-core indexer score path and its validated score-kernel priority policy without claiming specialized top-k or default-route integration.

cuda_oxide.module_form: executable-local #[cuda_module] eight-warp m16n8k16 indexer kernel plus pure Rust launch-order selector

covered_behavior: indexer_scores_wmma128_kernel 16-token by 128-component eight-warp tensor-core score tile
FP32-to-FP16 staged matrix inputs, positive-score weighting, scaling, and causal negative-infinity masking
validated-input score-kernel priority order: direct-one, WMMA128, WMMA64, WMMA32, base WMMA, scalar fallback
excluded_behavior: specialized power-of-two, CUB, chunked, merged, and tree top-k dispatch branches
runtime graph integration and default CUDA route

rust_owned_in_this_stage: validated-input current-C indexer score launch-priority policy
not_claimed_in_this_stage: runtime graph integration or default CUDA route
